C1.title: README's setsid non-claim is false: the child spawns descendants
C1.resolution: README process-group bullet rewritten to state the truth: the supervisor signals only the direct child PID, the fixture spawns no descendants so the matrix proves nothing about them, and the production child DOES spawn them via ingest_tracker/parse_tracker with start_new_session=True. Critic's proposed mitigation text was itself false and was NOT copied: verified at source that both trackers' shutdown() cancel only the asyncio wrapper and send the subprocess no signal, so descendants outlive the COOPERATIVE path too; killpg exists only on per-call wall-timeout paths. Guard: tests/test_desktop_contract.py::test_desktop_readme_never_claims_a_descendant_free_child (source-derived).

H1.title: `lsof` error is read as verified clean absence, violating AC3
H1.resolution: Probe discriminator rebuilt. _pid_is_gone now uses os.kill(pid,0) (ProcessLookupError=gone, PermissionError=alive), removing the subprocess that could misreport. _listener_lines opens a throwaway loopback listener and queries lsof about BOTH ports in ONE invocation; a reply omitting the control row raises. _probe_command also raises on exit-1-with-stderr and its stale found(0)/not-found(1) docstring is corrected. Demonstrated: with a stub lsof exiting 1 / empty stdout / empty stderr, the pre-fix helper returned [] for a port that WAS genuinely listening (vacuous pass); post-fix it raises 'lsof failed its positive control'. Guards: test_listener_probe_failure_raises_instead_of_reading_as_absence, test_probe_exit_one_with_diagnostics_is_an_error_not_a_no_match, test_pid_liveness_uses_signal_zero_rather_than_a_subprocess.

H3.title: ignore-shutdown arm can strand a SIGTERM-immune child
H3.source_axis: local-first + Docker constraint (no residue on the workstation)
H3.resolution: New _reaped_fault_supervisor context manager wraps every fault test: its finally stops the supervisor, SIGKILLs every child-spawn PID from the event log, and CONFIRMS each is gone within 5s. Backed by an eager _FAULT_CHILD_PIDS registry with a session-scoped autouse fixture and an atexit reaper for the Ctrl-C/interpreter-exit paths. Defense in depth (M3): the IgnoreShutdown arm now abort()s 60s after launch. Demonstrated: pre-fix teardown left the SIGTERM-immune fixture alive (measured, pid 42763); the M3 deadline fires at 60.1s with rc=-6 even with SIGTERM and stdin EOF both ignored. Guard: test_teardown_reaps_a_sigterm_immune_child_when_the_ladder_never_runs.

M1.title: Redaction is one call site, not the writer `redact.rs` claims
M1.resolution: redact.rs module doc restated to what is proven: coverage is CALL-SITE discipline at the single bound-frame-invalid site (Recorder::record does not scrub), child stderr is the Python RedactionFilter's responsibility, and any new child-derived event field MUST route through scrub. The 'two independent implementations' parity claim is replaced by the accurate one - a shared-vector LOCK requiring re-approval in Rust, in the Python reference semantic, and in fixtures.sha256 - since Python ships no production substring scrubber to compare against.

M4.title: 90s fault-test wait is shorter than the supervisor's own budget
M4.resolution: Budgets reconciled. _SUPERVISOR_WAIT_TIMEOUT=300s now exceeds the supervisor's own ~198s worst case (health 60 + ready 120 + smoke 15 + ladder) plus tauri boot, so a loaded box no longer times out without a bug - the timeout that was itself the H3 trigger. Duration is asserted from the event log's monotonic elapsed_ms via _ladder_ms(), which brackets shutdown_child exactly (lifecycle-failed -> orphan-shutdown), replacing the wall-clock 'wall < 30.0' that measured tauri boot and readiness polling while naming the ladder.

M8.title: Scrub runs at one call site, not at the persistence boundary
M8.resolution: DEFERRED: exceeds the MEDIUM 30-LOC bar and is a design change, not a rectification. Recorder::new(&root) runs in main() before any StartupToken exists - the token is generated per-cycle inside lifecycle.rs - so scrubbing inside record() needs a mutable token slot on the shared Recorder plus its set/clear lifecycle. M1's doc narrowing removes the misleading universal-coverage claim in the meantime and states the call-site obligation explicitly.

M11.title: AC3's "zero orphan process groups" has no pgid probe
M11.resolution: AC3's 'zero orphan process groups' is now measured, not argued. The 30-cycle stress captures os.getpgid(child) while the child is live and requires it to equal the harness's own group (a setsid() escape would differ), then requires the group rooted at the child's pid to be empty after teardown. New _pgid_members() reads the full process table (ps -A -o pid=,pgid=) instead of ps -g, which exits 1 for an empty group and a denied one alike, and raises unless its own pid appears. Guard: test_process_group_probe_requires_seeing_its_own_pid.
